# Congruences making `(36 n^3 - 19) / x` an integer
For each digit size `d` we give four *distinct* `d`-digit numbers `a1, b1, a2, b2` (in particular
`a1 ≠ b2`, as requested) such that
  x ≡ a1 (mod b1),  0 < x < b1,  and  n ≡ a2 (mod b2)   ⟹   x | 36 n^3 - 19.
All statements are proved in `RequestProject/Main.lean` (theorems `fraction_integer_d`,
digit counts in `digits_d`, an explicit satisfying pair in `witness_d`).
Construction: `a1 = p`, a prime with `p ≡ 2 (mod 3)`; `b1 = 2p`; `b2 = 3p`; and `a2` is a
solution of `36 a2^3 ≡ 19 (mod p)`, which exists because cubing is a bijection modulo such `p`.
Since `n ≡ a2 (mod 3p)` implies `n ≡ a2 (mod p)`, the divisibility `p | 36 n^3 - 19` follows.
The restriction `0 < x < b1` is not cosmetic: `no_full_residue_class` proves that for a fixed `n`
no infinite residue class of positive `x` can consist of divisors of the nonzero number
`36 n^3 - 19`. So `x` is pinned to the representative `a1` of its class, while `n` genuinely
ranges over the whole infinite class `a2 + b2 Z`.
